Eval 1 (pipe) was non-discriminating — both configs identically blocked by Bash permissions. Replace with a cartridge that has a pre-seeded CRITICAL flag.
Eval 0 (wall) showed a pass rate tie (both 80%) but with-skill was 3.2x faster (84s vs 272s) and used 40% fewer tokens — structured approach reduces wandering.
Eval 2 (mezzanine) showed clearest skill advantage: with-skill found 3 invalid phys values beyond task scope; without-skill declared clean after narrower check.
Critical gap: neither agent caught the FUZZ_CRASH in the wall (tag_socket on deleted face) — skill should enforce running AUDIT before static analysis since crashes only surface at runtime.
Skill adds 0.07 mean pass rate improvement but delivers larger benefits in token efficiency (-27% tokens) and time (-46% time) by providing structured workflow.
